text: A man stood on a railroad bridge. <break time="0.8s" /> In northern Alabama. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking down into the swift water. <break time="0.8s" /> Twenty feet below. <break time="0.8s" /> His hands tied behind his back. <break time="0.8s" /> A rope around his neck. <break time="0.8s" /> Was fastened to a beam above his head. <break time="0.8s" /> And he stood on a loose board. <break time="0.8s" /> Laid across the railroad ties. <break time="0.8s" /> Two Union soldiers and their sergeant. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood beside him on the board. <break time="0.8s" /> And nearby stood a captain. <break time="0.8s" /> Who watched quietly. <break time="0.8s" /> With his arms folded. <break time="0.8s" /> At each end of the bridge. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood a guard. <break time="0.8s" /> With his rifle held straight up. <break time="0.8s" /> In front of his chest. <break time="0.8s" /> The man who was about to die. <break time="0.8s" /> Was about thirty five years old. <break time="0.8s" /> And he was dressed like a rich planter. <break time="0.8s" /> Not like a soldier. <break time="0.8s" /> When he closed his eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> To think of his wife and children. <break time="0.8s" /> A sharp, ringing sound. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a hammer striking iron. <break time="0.8s" /> Broke into his thoughts. <break time="0.8s" /> It was only the ticking of his watch. <break time="0.8s" /> But each tick. <break time="0.8s" /> Seemed slower and louder. <break time="0.8s" /> Than the one before. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a wild hope came to him. <break time="0.8s" /> That he might free his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> Throw off the rope. <break time="0.8s" /> And swim home to his family. <break time="0.8s" /> Just as these thoughts. <break time="0.8s" /> Flashed through his mind. <break time="0.8s" /> The captain nodded to the sergeant. <break time="0.8s" /> And the sergeant stepped off the board.
